rv.q: This play is, ironically, full of life, even though there are struggles and tears.
This is a mesmerizing portrait of how an earth-shattering personal tragedy can effect the others in our lives.

The magic of "The Luckiest," directed sensitively and with an eye for fine detail by Cody Estle, is that even though the first minutes of play foreshadow how the drama will unfold, it remains fully compelling, engrossing until the final, inevitable blackout.
I must tell you that this production, sharply directed by Artistic Director Cody Estle surprised me to no end.

cn.t: Critics praise this emotionally potent Chicago premiere about friendship and mortality, with Melissa Ross's sharp writing and Cody Estle's direction earning acclaim for confronting death with surprising humor and heart.
